title: Introduce hierarchical token cost atlas and alert fallthrough policy
author: Asha Kapoor
release_notes: Adds a hierarchical token cost atlas for per-tenant/route/invocation attribution; new dashboards and an alert fallthrough policy to reduce noisy long-tail SLO pages. Feature gated; no behavior change until enabled.
description:
Motivation: Long-tail token cost + latency noise makes SLO paging noisy for routes with highly variable prompt shapes. Existing token-level metrics are flat and expensive to query when you want to slice by route -> model-stage -> tenant. This PR introduces a compact, hierarchical token cost atlas to make per-segment attribution fast and shippable to dashboards/alerts.

Goals: 1) provide a compact index (atlas) that aggregates token cost/latency by hierarchical keys (tenant, route, model_stage, segment_shingle) while remaining query-friendly; 2) power a conservative alert fallthrough policy that escalates pages only when multiple hierarchy levels show correlated degradation; 3) minimize runtime overhead using sketch summaries and reservoir rollups; 4) expose a Console viewer and Grafana-ready panels for exploration.

What this change does: single continuous implementation across the telemetry pipeline: (a) a changed telemetry collector that emits atlas records (compact sketches + top-k signatures) to the metric store; (b) a lightweight span enricher that attaches atlas_signature and token.bucket_id to long-running spans; (c) an aggregation service that materializes daily/rolling atlas rollups; (d) dashboard JSON for the Console and Grafana panels: Token Cost Atlas, Atlas Explorer, and Route Correlator; (e) new alerting policy engine additions implementing the fallthrough logic (alert groups with progressive sensitivity and correlation windowing).

Backward compatibility & rollout: The feature is behind an observability feature flag (obs.hierarchical_token_atlas). When disabled nothing is emitted. New metric names are under the redwood.atlas.* namespace. Migration steps are in docs/observability/hierarchical-token-atlas.md. We coordinate retention changes with infra; default retention unchanged.

Performance & cost: Microbenchmarks show ~3-5% CPU on collector when atlas is enabled for high-traffic clusters; we use count-min sketches and a fixed-size reservoir to bound memory and cardinality. Integration tests include a synthetic replaybench (tests/atlas_integration_test.go) exercising worst-case cardinality.

Rollout plan: Feature-flag rollout to internal canary -> tenant opt-in in Console -> enable by default for Dedicated in 2 weeks if no regressions.

Risks & mitigations: Risk of label explosion mitigated by signature shingling and atlas bucketization; alert noise avoided using fallthrough groups and correlation windows.

Notes: This PR intentionally keeps the atlas writer and downstream query API separate so dashboards can be swapped to other stores later. More follow-ups planned: automated atlas compaction, per-tenant retention tuning, and a small SDK addition to pull atlas slices for offline evals.

Jordan Liu: High level LGTM, please add perf numbers to the docs and ensure the sketch parameters are tunable at runtime.

Asha (author): Added perf section to docs and runtime knobs via collector config.

Marco Santoro: The metric namespace looks fine but please avoid adding high-cardinality labels to the base metrics. Can we move tenant->route tagging into the atlas metadata instead of label on every datapoint?

Asha: Changed the collector to keep route/tenant as atlas metadata; only atlas_signature and bucket_id get attached to spans. Removed high-cardinality labels from base metrics.

Sofia Reyes: Can we add a small integration test that simulates a multi-tenant burst to validate memory bounds?

Asha: Added tests/atlas_integration_test.go and a replay script that runs in the CI "telemetry-integration" job.

Marco: One nit on naming: suggest atlas_bucket -> token.bucket_id. Applied.

Jordan: Approved after a green CI run.
